newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Petroz agrees Timor Sea well farm-out.
newsitem.headline: Petroz agrees Timor Sea well farm-out.

text.p: Oil junior Petroz NL said on Friday it has agreed terms for the farm-out of a half-interest in its planned Schilling-1 exploration well in the Timor Sea.
Petroz said it estimates the Schilling prospect could hold potential oil reserves for the four-way closure of 32 million barrels, and a high side of 50 million barrels.
Potential reserves for the higher risk fault closure were estimated at a mean of 255 million barrels and a high side of 490 million barrels, the company said.
The prospect is located in exploration permit WA-74-P in the central part of the Timor Sea, offshore northwest Australia.

Under the farm-out agreement, Idemitsu Oil & Gas, Magellan Petroleum Corp, Norwest Energy and Premier Oil will earn a 50 percent interest in the permit in exchange for contributing to the costs of the Schilling-1 well.
Petroz said the well would test both the four-way dip closure and a larger fault dependant closure.
The well would be drilled in 108 metres of water to a total depth of about 3,200 metres.
